correctness.rationale: The quartic chord Fourier endpoint asymptotic has coefficient 4√2 Γ(5/4) and power t^-5/4; the beta area normalization yields pole 5√π. Quartic finite-type stationary phase gives the uniform scaling t^-5/4(1+|θ| t^3/4)^-1/3, and the bounded-parameter expansion plus integrable tail gives angular logarithm factor 4/3. Smooth positive-curvature stationary phase yields nonaxial threshold p=3, and polar-area integration with the uniform bound proves the noncompact finite-area interval. The checker passed 17 finite diagnostics, with no finite-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: The exact quartic disk is a natural first intermediate finite-type test for the 2026 Fourier-mean construction. Its index 5/2, sharp 20√π/3 log horn, 5√π axial residue and unbounded-yet-finite-area phase distinguish geometric compactness from area integrability. The two-parameter horn law, not merely a generic Fourier decay estimate, is the structurally informative part.
